2 · Paste the post copy

Daily, at a site called The Daily Anchorage, means July 8th to July 26th.
Nothing since. More than 500 stories are still live on August 13th.

The form is all there. Politics, property, schools, transport. A corrections page and legal notices. No named reporter appears anywhere.

Bylines go to desks. Each article checked says it "was not reviewed by a journalist before publishing."

The about page promises to disclose AI involvement on every page, and it does. It asks readers to verify anything important.

The deck sets the tagline against the dates and lists the network's 18 mastheads, all Australian. Anchorage is not one.

Every part of a newsroom is here except the part that does the reporting.

Does full disclosure earn a page the word local, or does that still need a person who can be asked about the story?

#AlaskaMedia #NewsDeserts #AIDisclosure

3 · Post, then paste this as the FIRST comment (within a minute)

Editor's note

SCORE 8.08 AGAINST A THRESHOLD OF 8.3. SHIPPED WITH A DISCLOSED SHORTFALL. No hard fail survives and the scorer says plainly that the deck is postable and that it would not block on defect grounds. The 0.22 gap is process, not defect.

THE SHORTFALL, stated first because it is the thing to know. This deck ran ZERO pixel-critic rounds and NO flow-critic round. Every slide was reviewed at full size by the showrunner and the deck as a sequence on the contact sheet, which caught two real text collisions and an engraved-lay artifact, but a single scorer is the only independent review this deck received. That is the second time in three decks those two rooms were skipped, No.30 did the same, and the first scoring cycle found two HARD FAILS that are exactly the class of defect those rooms exist to catch.

THE TWO HARD FAILS, both on slide 08, both repaired and both verified in the pixels by the second scoring pass. A canvas label was clipped at the right frame edge, printing MORE THAN 20. TWO READS DISA instead of MORE THAN 20. TWO READS DISAGREED. C28. That severed string was the deck honesty device, the sentence explaining why the slide says more than 20 instead of a count, so losing it made the deck look like it was asserting a number it had deliberately refused to assert. The second was the body copy last word landing on a slug light-on-light. Neither was visible to any machine gate, because canvas has no layout engine.

THE MACHINE UPGRADE CAME OUT OF THAT. render.py now records where canvas text actually lands and qa.py FAILS a string whose span leaves the frame. Verified three ways, a reconstruction of the defect fails at 147px past the edge, the repaired deck renders 9 of 9 clean, and the bespoke reference deck stays clean so there is no false positive. It closes the clipping half of this failure family. It does NOT close the other half, DOM text landing on lit canvas art, which is still caught by eye alone.

THE STANDING WEAKNESS MOVED BUT DID NOT CLOSE. Artwork craft had been weakest in 7 of the last 10 runs at a mean of 6.0. This run used akengrave, the engraver bench that five consecutive decks had left unused, and drawn share went from a 23 percent templated baseline to 99 percent. Four frames genuinely improved, and the scorer named slide 02 500-ribbon proof stack the best-drawn object this studio has shipped. Artwork craft still scored 6, level with its own mean, because five frames carry flat regions. Drawn is not the same as modelled. The one-sentence fix for next time is on slide 08 two comparison slugs.

THREE THINGS BEFORE YOU POST. Slide 06 prints JUL 8 TO JUL 26. CHECKED AUGUST 13TH, which mixes the abbreviated stamp form with the ordinal prose form in one string; caption_check passed it as a provenance stamp but it is worth your ruling. Slide 07 vermilion stamp does not read at feed size. And two annotation strings were restored AFTER the final score and are therefore unscored, slide 07 C21 line and slide 08 tracker as-of date; both are strictly additive and qa.py re-ran clean.

WHAT THE ADVERSARIAL PASS KILLED. The scouts offered a second leg, a doctored image of a gubernatorial candidate circulating before the primary. The fact-checker searched the outlet twice, got 61 results in strict date order with a clean gap across the claimed publication date, and could not find it. Nothing about it is in this deck. Two counts also would not reproduce, so the deck ships floors and prints the non-reproducibility on the slides.

SITE SIGN-OFF: PASS, 75 pages, 18 checks.
GAS WATCH: PASS, read 2026-08-12, 8 days on record, chart present.
SITE FIXES: rebuilt docs/ twice, once after the docket refresh left it stale and once to resolve a merge with the gas watch cron by regenerating rather than hand-editing generated files. Also fixed the ask-engine test, which was reading an Anchorage-built page on a UTC clock and going red whenever a docket date landed in the eight-hour gap between the two calendars.

Automation changes this run (1)

The routine modified its own machinery this run. If a later week looks worse, this dated section is the rollback trail (each set reverts as one commit).
KindChangeRollback
fix
engine, render.py and qa.py		Canvas text is now measured where it lands, and qa.py FAILS a string that runs off the frame. render.py's init-script hook already recorded every fillText/strokeText string; it now also records the draw coordinates, the measured advance, textAlign, the active transform and the canvas size, and computes the string's device-space left and right edges. qa.py adds a canvas-bounds check that fails when a meaningful string (4 or more alphabetic characters) ends past the right edge or starts left of the frame.
why: Run No.32 slide 08 shipped the label 'MORE THAN 20. TWO READS DISAGREED. C28' starting at x 830 with 38 characters to draw in 250px. The render printed 'MORE THAN 20. TWO READS DISA		git revert the upgrade(2026-08-13) commit. The hook fields are additive and default to absent, so an older render_report still parses and the check simply skips entries without dev_right.

Aftercare (this is where reach is won)

  • Post Tuesday to Thursday, 8am to 11am Alaska time.
  • Paste the first comment immediately, inside the first minute, so the sources land with the post.
  • Reply to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes. Threaded author replies are the strongest reach lever this page has.
  • If a commenter asks whether the site is illegal, the honest answer is that it disclosed and Alaska has no law on this. That is the deck's point.
  • Do not name the founder in replies. The deck deliberately carries the absence of a registered legal entity instead.
  • Do not link the site in a comment. Describing it is enough and a link rewards it.
